node_completion_findings.finding: This node's responsibilities include 'documentation' and it writes a new fact document (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-24-image-sessions-design.md), but the workflow node carries no `required_documents` field. This project's own tooling (.allforai/bootstrap/scripts/evidence_freshness.py) reads `node.get('required_documents', [])` as one of its two document sources for dependency and freshness tracking. Practical impact is muted here because the same document is already listed under `exit_artifacts` with validation_commands (which evidence_freshness.py also scans), so dependency/freshness tracking is not actually broken — but the schema's dedicated document-contract field is empty, which is exactly the condition the audit skill names as `missing_document_contract`.

attention_management_findings.finding: The node's Attention Contract prose (Must-read inputs, Stop Conditions) requires `.allforai/image-sessions/backend-report.json` to exist and be `status: passed` before this node may proceed ('后端 backend-report.json 为 passed... 任一缺失 → blocked'). The structured `source_inputs` array — the field the execution harness uses for bootstrap-context-compression pull-mode reading — does not list this file at all, only the design doc and local-requirements.json plus static frontend source files. A pull-mode executor that reads exactly `source_inputs` (as the philosophy prescribes) has no mechanical way to discover or check the backend gate.
